headline: Highest risk is medium: OpenMetadata’s MCP/API/webhook surfaces can cascade or conflict with nuwa-skill’s allowlisted egress, but no shared workspace or direct injection path is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between nuwa-skill and OpenMetadata. nuwa-skill shows only allowlisted network egress, while OpenMetadata exposes APIs/SDKs/events/webhooks/MCP; without a bridge, prompt injection via one agent’s outputs into the other is not evidenced.
conditions: IF an orchestrator forwards nuwa-skill output into OpenMetadata prompts or MCP calls, injection risk becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added, the pathway changes from none to at least low.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected except through typed, schema-validated fields.
Disable any automatic prompt forwarding between tools.
Review any MCP bridge for provenance tags before enabling it.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing for any future bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, semantics, and memory/tribal knowledge, so it may handle sensitive metadata. nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress, but no shared workspace or direct file-sharing surface is documented, so leakage is possible only if an operator connects them through a common channel.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or metadata store, leakage risk increases.
IF OpenMetadata is configured to ingest or export sensitive metadata to external APIs, data can leave the boundary.
mitigations: Keep sensitive datasets out of any shared workspace.
Restrict OpenMetadata connectors to non-sensitive sources.
Audit outbound destinations for OpenMetadata before enabling them.
Use separate credentials for each agent.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenMetadata supports multiple instances and uses APIs/SDKs/events/webhooks/MCP, so it can contend over shared mutable resources. nuwa-skill’s allowlisted egress does not prevent conflicts if both are pointed at the same backend or metadata target; the interaction is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty is escalated.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same metadata backend or API namespace, concurrent updates can conflict.
IF either agent mutates shared records without locking, lost updates become possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate namespace.
Turn on optimistic locking where available.
Schedule writes so only one agent updates a resource at a time.
Review API write scopes before enabling both agents.
requires-engineering: add transaction or lock coordination around shared writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata is a data-catalog/context layer, so it can treat upstream outputs as authoritative metadata. If nuwa-skill produces incorrect facts and OpenMetadata ingests them through APIs, events, or MCP, errors can cascade into lineage and governance views; no verification step is documented here.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill-generated facts are ingested into OpenMetadata without validation, downstream records can be wrong.
IF OpenMetadata is used as a source of truth for other systems, the error propagates further.
mitigations: Require human review before ingesting new facts.
Mark nuwa-skill outputs as untrusted provenance.
Compare outputs against a second source before publishing.
Limit OpenMetadata writes to draft or staging records.
requires-engineering: add automated validation against source systems.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance and lineage data classes that can carry regulated metadata, while nuwa-skill’s profile does not specify residency or retention controls. Because the pair’s compliance posture is undocumented and OpenMetadata can move data through APIs/webhooks/MCP, a mismatch is plausible and uncertainty should be treated conservatively.
conditions: IF regulated metadata is stored in OpenMetadata and exported through external APIs, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF nuwa-skill is used on data subject to stricter residency or retention rules, the pair may violate policy.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent.
Disable external webhooks for regulated datasets.
Review retention settings in OpenMetadata.
Use region-scoped deployments for sensitive data.
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement for residency and retention.
